text:
maria: seeing controller-manager leader flip in us-west-2 over the last 7m, apiserver returning intermittent 503s, and GPU pods are stuck Pending. anyone seeing control-plane noise?

liam: saw alerts too. grafana shows control-plane e2e latency spikes and etcd request lat p95 up ~3x.

ken: quick check: `kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide` shows controller-manager restarting on cp-uw2a-02 and cp-uw2b-01.

maria: pasted controller-manager stderr snippet:
```
I0305 10:14:22.123456 1 leaderelection.go:243] failed to renew lease: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
W0305 10:14:22.123458 1 leaderelection.go:330] failed to update lock: context deadline exceeded
```

anita: DeadlineExceeded from leader election usually network or apiserver slowness. also saw kube-apiserver logs with slow response to watch requests.

sre-bot: [ALERT] control-plane-leader-flap us-west-2 - 3 occurrences in 10m.

liam: could be VPC route flap between AZs? cloud provider also shows a networking event in us-west-2b around 10:12.

ken: confirmed: `ip route` on cp-uw2a-02 had transient route withdraw for 172.20.0.0/16 to cp-uw2b-01 while kubelet heartbeats failed.

maria: result = controllers can't acquire leases -> leader elections, which bounces controller-manager -> controllers re-enqueue lots of work -> API load spikes -> apiserver starts returning 503s under load.

anita: and that causes cluster-autoscaler to spin up GPU nodes which then get stuck because apiserver timing out when creating PVCs. it's a cascading failure.

liam: quick mitigations I vote for:
- mark GPU nodepool AZs in us-west-2b as unschedulable for new pods (taint)
- pin controller-manager leader to a stable node if possible (not ideal)
- open cloud support ticket for the AZ networking blip

maria: applied taint to gpu-pool-uw2b: `kubectl taint nodes -l pool=gpu-usw2b avoid-new-gpu=true:NoSchedule`

ken: also bumped etcd client timeouts for controller-manager? not yet. maybe increase leader election durations temporarily to reduce churn: `--leader-elect-renew-deadline=20s` -> `30s` on kube-controller-manager.

anita: careful — increasing election timeouts trades faster failover for stability. fine for mitigation window. I can push a short-lived deploy patch to kube-controller-manager with increased timeouts and extra logging.

deploy-bot: deploy started: kube-controller-manager@patch-raise-leaderelect -> staging -> monitoring for 5m.

maria: after taint + timeout bump, leader flips dropped to 1 in 10m and apiserver 503 rate down by ~80%. PVC create backlog is draining.

liam: followups:
- open a postmortem to track root cause (network route propagation)
- evaluate adding cross-AZ control-plane peering routes and BGP health checks
- add a canary for leader-election churn in our control-plane SLOs
- look at autoscaler guardrails so it doesn't add GPUs during control-plane instability

ken: also check etcd disk latency metrics. if etcd iops were high it would amplify leader-election failures. put a small note to check `etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration` in the window.

anita: creating incident ticket: INC-2026 - us-west-2 control-plane leader churn + GPU scheduling cascade. linking logs and grafana.

maria: thanks all. marking this thread resolved for now, will follow up in INC-2026 postmortem with action owners. :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: [NOTE] Incident created INC-2026 by anita. Assigned: maria, liam, ken.
